importance: data_table is the most important field. It contains pre-computed, chart-ready data that the Programmer inlines directly into Vega-Lite charts. The Programmer does NOT have access to the raw data — this is their only data source.
when_to_include: For every finding, ask: 'Could a chart show this?' If yes, include a data_table with the full aggregated values.

patterns.trend: e.g. 'registrations grew 4.5x' → data_table with year-by-year counts.
patterns.group_comparison: e.g. 'industry posts at 19.8% vs academic 10.0%' → data_table with ALL groups and their rates.
patterns.ranking: e.g. 'Breast Cancer is #1 with 152 trials' → data_table with ALL ranked items, not just top-N.
patterns.distribution: e.g. '94.2% have no phase' → data_table with all category counts and percentages.
patterns.anomaly_or_single_scalar: e.g. 'median is 160' → no data_table needed; the content field carries the value.

include_all_values: Include ALL values, not just the highlighted one. If the finding says 'neurological has the highest gain at 16.1%', the data_table should include ALL categories with their values. The Designer may show all, highlight one, or filter.

format.description: one-line description of what this table contains.
format.rows: array of arrays (each inner array = one row, positional with columns).

maps_to_vega_lite: columns + rows → [{"col1": val1, "col2": val2}, ...]. Compact (important for token budget) and maps directly to Vega-Lite inline data.
